channel.title: Writings — Suraj Sharma, XO Labs
channel.description: Long-form research on agentic systems and the measurement of work.

item.title: Kafka, taken apart, part 1: The log on disk
item.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 1: the partition directory, the record batch byte by byte, an append that does not sync, sparse offset and time indexes, record-time rolls and retention, compaction and tombstones, and log recovery under hand-injected damage.

item.title: Kafka, taken apart, part 2: One request, on the wire and through the broker
item.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 2: the broker's thread pools and request queue, the muted socket, a real Produce frame decoded byte by byte, purgatory and the timing wheel, quota throttling, generated protocol schemas, and ApiVersions negotiation.

item.title: Kafka, taken apart, part 3: What an ack promises: replication and the metadata quorum
item.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 3: the commit ladder, what an acks=all ack promises, the two ways out of the ISR, leader epochs and truncation, ELR and last-known-leader election, the KRaft metadata log, controller failover, and what quorum loss stops.

item.title: Kafka, taken apart, part 4: Producers and consumer groups
item.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 4: the producer's accumulator and Sender, linger and batch size, partitioners across clients, idempotence and where it runs out, consumer position and commits, classic and KIP-848 rebalances, static membership and share groups.

item.title: Kafka, taken apart, part 5: Exactly-once, as it is
item.description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 5: the transaction coordinator, TV2, control markers on disk, the last stable offset, epoch fencing, hanging transactions and KAFKA-20734, what exactly-once does not cover, and the collection's findings register.

item.title: Terraform, taken apart, part 1: The language and the front end
item.description: Terraform v1.17.0 taken apart, part 1: HCL's scanner and parser, schema-driven decoding, cty values with unknowns and marks, the block schemas, directory loading, the init graph and early evaluation, and provider installation with the lock file.

item.title: Terraform, taken apart, part 2: The engine and the providers
item.description: Terraform v1.17.0's engine and provider protocol read from the source: the plan-graph transformer pipeline, the DAG walker and -parallelism, count/for_each expansion, the per-instance plan and -minimal-refresh, provider processes and the go-plugin handshake, tfplugin6 and cty msgpack on the wire, saved plan files and the apply re-plan. Part 2 of Terraform, taken apart.

item.title: Terraform, taken apart, part 3: State, refactoring and the feature arc
item.description: Terraform v1.17.0 taken apart, part 3: the v4 state file, lineage and serial, locks per backend and the S3 default with no lock, workspaces and terraform_remote_state, moved/removed/import blocks, and the 1.5 to 1.17 features from check and terraform test to ephemeral values, query, actions, deferral, Stacks and Policy.

item.title: Terraform, taken apart, part 4: Building on three clouds, and the ecosystem
item.description: Terraform v1.17.0 in its ecosystem and on three clouds: the BUSL licence and what stayed MPL, OpenTofu v1.13.2 measured (provider for_each and state encryption as one-way doors), Stacks and Policy as out-of-process plugins, a multicloud AWS/GCP/Azure project planned and tested with no credentials, write-only database passwords end to end, mock providers, local policy failing open, and the 101-item findings register. Part 4 of Terraform, taken apart.

item.title: Docker, taken apart, part 1: From docker run to a process
item.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 1: the docker run call sequence, OCI spec generation, containerd and the runc-v2 shim, runc's nsexec stages and 40-byte bootstrap message, the create/start FIFO, and the exit path.

item.title: Docker, taken apart, part 2: Images, layers and the registry
item.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 2: the OCI image as a tree of hashes, digest vs DiffID vs ChainID, tar layers and whiteouts, a measured Docker Hub pull, credentials, containerd's content store and snapshots, the two image stores, and a local registry's push path and GC.

item.title: Docker, taken apart, part 3: How BuildKit builds
item.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 and BuildKit v0.34.1 taken apart, part 3: docker build as buildx over gRPC, the Dockerfile frontend and # syntax=, LLB as a protobuf Merkle DAG reproduced from alpine's provenance, the solver's fast and slow cache keys, context transfer, RUN mounts and the runc executor, and exporters, cache export and attestations.

item.title: Docker, taken apart, part 4: Networks, I/O and the long run
item.description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 4: port publishing as DNAT plus docker-proxy, the iptables and nftables chains, the embedded DNS server at 127.0.0.11, the stdcopy frame and the log pipeline, stop, kill and restart policies, health, OOM, stats and events, the 2013-2026 history, and the full register of 100 findings.

item.title: Git, taken apart, part 1: The commit and its objects
item.description: Git v2.55.0 taken apart, part 1: one traced commit, loose object bytes and names, the object lookup chain, pack deltas, .idx fanout lookup, and reachability bitmaps, with measured numbers.

item.title: Git, taken apart, part 2: Mutable state and the wire
item.description: Git's mutable state and transport, read from the git 2.55 source: the index format and racy git, lock timeouts, refs and reftable, atomic-but-not-durable publishing, pkt-lines and protocol v2, fetch negotiation and the push quarantine. Part 2 of Git, taken apart.

item.title: Git, taken apart, part 3: Combining, keeping, and how it got here
item.description: Git v2.55.0 taken apart, part 3: merge bases and generation numbers, merge-ort, rename detection, conflict styles and rerere, auto-maintenance and geometric repack, prune's grace period, the commit-graph and Bloom filters, history to Git 3.0, and a findings register with reproductions.

item.title: One repository, many agents
item.description: Git worktrees read from git v2.55.0 and measured: what is shared, what is private, the one-branch rule, prune, sparse checkout and partial clone, and a tested recipe for running many agents on one repository.

item.title: Parsing bash, taken apart
item.description: GNU bash parses with a Bison grammar only because its lexer reads parser state, re-enters the parser for each $( ) and leaves words as text for expansion. A teardown of bash@9c46586 from bytes to fork, set beside five other shell parsers on 148 tricky inputs and a 100,000-line script.

item.title: Next.js routing, taken apart
item.description: Next.js 16.4 turns an app/ folder tree into a sorted route table, server entries, prerendered segment files and prefetch hints before the first request. A teardown that follows one route from file to click through the code at v16.4.0, and prices each precomputation with measured numbers.

item.title: Anatomy of GitHub CLI
item.description: How gh works, what you can call, where its data lives, and which system owns the result: commands, YAML configuration, accounts, credentials, Git, REST, GraphQL, Projects, Actions, extensions, agents, and a durable adapter for a session operating system.

item.title: What Each File Wants
item.description: No best compressor, only the right match. A measured field guide to compressing JSON, small messages, config files, logs, tables, images, audio and video in October 2026 — which codec, which level or quality, when a format beats a compressor, and when to leave a file alone.

item.title: What Compression Keeps
item.description: Compression keeps all the information in fewer bits; compaction keeps only the present. A long explainer of both — entropy, coders, the 2026 codecs, prediction, lossy coding, HTTP and attacks, then LSM trees, Kafka, VACUUM, GC, git gc and agent context compaction — measured and compared side by side.

item.title: What the Parser Hears
item.description: A configuration file has two readers. A field guide to JSON, YAML and TOML as configuration formats in October 2026 — their specs, every pitfall that still bites, what 34 real parsers hear for the same 71 inputs, and a practice for choosing and guarding a config format.

item.title: What is a TOML file?
item.description: How a plain-text .toml file becomes structured data, and how a program turns that data into behavior: keys, tables, types, parsing, validation, overrides, version compatibility, and the configuration boundary for a session operating system.

item.title: Codex JSON, field by field
item.description: A recursive reference to .codex-global-state.json: every observed object shape becomes a folder, and every leaf gets a section. Covers field meanings, writes, project and thread links, cached schemas, and the boundary for a session operating system.

item.title: Turborepo or Nx
item.description: Both now call themselves the build system for coding agents. A sourced comparison of Turborepo 2.11 and Nx 23.2 — graph models, cache keys, remote caching, distributed CI, polyglot support, governance, agent features, pricing and supply-chain history — with a benchmark of both on one workspace.

item.title: Where the JSON Lives
item.description: Relational versus non-relational is the wrong first question. A field guide to both families, the 2024–2026 licence ledger, best practices that survive production, and a measured answer to where JSON that is loaded and stored all day should live — built from free, open-source parts.

item.title: A Table With Two Columns
item.description: A page registry is a table: a shape name in your data on the left, the code allowed to draw it on the right. The three shapes a page can have, six ways to build the lookup, what one entry must carry, where to validate, how to version against two deploy clocks — and where MagicPath fits, with an honest ledger.

item.title: Nothing Runs While You're Gone
item.description: A build timer is one integer on one row. It is also the cheapest server design for a game with a hundred million players, and the mechanism that decides when you next open the app. How the two halves are the same object — and where that stops being a fair trade.

item.title: The State Is Enough
item.description: A Markov process is a bet: that you can choose a description of "now" so complete that the past adds nothing. What that bet buys, and where computer science cashes it — PageRank, MCMC, Viterbi, Kalman, MDPs, branch predictors, queueing, and the state-size fight between attention and state-space models.

item.title: Anatomy of a Codex session
item.description: What a Codex session contains, how it runs, where it persists, and how to control it: threads, turns, items, projects, commands, permissions, forks, SDKs, and background execution. A versioned anatomy for designing an operating system that can route work into Space and other products.

item.title: Anatomy of a Claude Code session
item.description: What a Claude Code session is made of, read from the 2.1.280 binary and measured on one machine: four identities, nine boot steps, the transcript graph, 120 options, the state file every process rewrites, 66 control requests, seven doors, and the friction map for building an OS around it.

item.title: Blink, taken apart
item.description: Chromium's rendering engine read end to end at commit f288fed6 (Chrome 156.0.8067.0): the tree and its DEPS-enforced layering, the process and thread model, the RenderingNG pipeline, Oilpan on cppgc, Web IDL bindings, runtime-enabled features and web tests.

item.title: DEPS, gclient and what replaced goma
item.description: A teardown of Chromium's dependency machine: depot_tools, the DEPS grammar, gclient sync step by step, submodules, autorollers, toolchain pinning — and goma, reclient and Siso.

item.title: The tree that configures the fleet
item.description: A teardown of Chromium's CI/CD: the LUCI stack, infra/config Starlark and the generated cfgs, tests on bots, bot_update, the commit queue, tree closers and gardeners, the two-week release cycle and the release scripts.

item.title: Liveblocks, read for XO Space
item.description: What Liveblocks is, where a room-per-project would sit inside xo-space, whether it installs inside the container (the SDKs do, the room server does not), and what autonomous building and sharing of a Space would actually mean — with a bounded pilot.

item.title: The ten hardest open problems in mathematics
item.description: Ten problems, ranked by how much of mathematics moves when they move — what each claims, what is actually proved as of August 2026, where mathematics is genuinely NP-hard or undecidable, how many kinds of infinity there are, and a dated forecast of which problems fall by 2050.

item.title: XO Space: the architecture
item.description: The implementation reference for xo-space: install and run, the xo-project folder contract, and the full data model — every entity collected, what bounds each file, and where the plane duplicates itself.

item.title: The J-Space: a construction manual
item.description: What the Jacobian Lens is, why averaging is the whole trick, and exactly how to build a J-space — compute routes, sparse decomposition, read and write operations, and a validation protocol.

item.title: One Graph, No Boxes
item.description: A close reading of Click and Paleczny's 1995 paper, the origin of the Sea of Nodes — every figure redrawn — and the general recipe inside it for representing any process over any data.

item.title: The Sea of Nodes, explained simply
item.description: A plain-language explanation of the program representation behind V8's TurboFan: three kinds of edges, why pure instructions float, how the graph becomes a program again, and why V8 left it.

item.title: Anatomy of an Agent Control Plane
item.description: A teardown of xo-space, the local control plane for AI coding agents: one capability seam, agents declared as data, four transports under one streaming contract, and a session index that holds no messages.

item.title: Anatomy of a Personal Memory Engine
item.description: A component-by-component teardown of iai-pme, a fully local memory engine for coding agents: fail-safe capture hooks, an encrypted verbatim store, a vector index that isn't HNSW, and nightly consolidation.

item.title: What is a unit of work?
item.description: A prompt asks for an action. A unit of work owns an outcome from definition through verification. The quirq is the proposed unit for measuring that verified work.

item.title: quirq: A Unit of Work for Intelligence
item.description: The token meters what AI consumes. The quirq is proposed as the output meter: budgeted by an owner, minted by verification, costed all-in, read as a trajectory.
